scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 1, verses 11.1.4–11.1.5.

entries.sanskrit: तर्हीदम् अप्य् अन्यैर् घात्यतां ? तत्राह---नैवेति । अन्यतो देवादिभ्योऽपि यादव-कुलस्य परिभवस् तिरस्कारो न भवेत् । कुतः ? मत्-संश्रयस्य मां संश्रयत इति मत्-संश्रयं कुलं तस्य । किं च, नित्यं विभवोन्नहनस्य विभवैर् गज-तुरगादिभिर् उच्छृङ्खलस्य । यद् वा, तर्हीदं किम् इति संहर्तव्यं ? तत्राह---विभवोन्नहनस्येति । तस्माद् एवं करिष्यामीत्य् आह---अन्तः कलिम् इति । शान्तिम् उपशमम् उपैमि, वर्तमान-सामीप्ये वर्तमानवद् व उपैष्यामि । तद्-अनन्तरं धाम च वैकुण्ठाख्यम् उपैष्यामीत्य् अर्थः ॥४॥
word_for_word: let it be killed by others
of what takes refuge in me
then why should this be brought to an end?
to this he replies with ‘unrestrained through affluence’
a present-tense form used for an imminent future action
entries.literal_english: Then why not have others kill this dynasty as well? The verse answers, ‘Certainly not’: even gods and others could not humiliate the Yadu family, because it takes refuge in me. Moreover, it is constantly unrestrained through wealth such as elephants and horses. Alternatively, one may ask why it should be ended at all; the answer is precisely that it is unrestrained through its wealth. Therefore, the Lord says he will cause strife within it and then attain peace or cessation. The present form ‘I attain’ denotes the imminent future, ‘I shall attain’; afterward he will attain the abode called Vaikuṇṭha.
entries.note: Śrīdhara offers two alternatives concerning the dynasty's wealth. ‘Śānti’ is glossed as upaśama, not silently substituted with another commentator's interpretation of destruction.

entries.literal_english: ‘Resolved’ means having made a firm decision. ‘He gathered back’ means he brought to an end.
entries.note: The source attributes only this brief two-part gloss to Śrīdhara; later explanations belong to Jīva and Viśvanātha, not Śrīdhara.
